openingPositionRules.anchoring: Always present the Executive/premium tier first in proposals. This sets the psychological reference point. Clients moving down feel they are saving; clients moving up feel they are spending extra.
openingPositionRules.premiumFirst: A client who reviews the $180k Executive package and agrees to the $120k Professional feels they made a smart decision. A client shown the $80k Foundation first and asked to upgrade to $120k feels they are being upsold.

threeOptionsFramework.buyerBehaviour: 65–70% choose the middle option when 3 tiers are clearly presented
threeOptionsFramework.naming: Never use Option A/B/C. Always use identity-based names that create aspiration.

closingTechniques.silenceClose: After presenting final pricing, do not fill the silence. The first person to speak is in the weaker position. Wait for the client to respond.
closingTechniques.uncertaintyClose: 'What would need to be true for you to feel confident moving forward?' — surfaces unstated objections without pressure.
closingTechniques.certaintyClose: Once client approves design, reinforce the cost of inaction: lead times, installation slot availability. This is not manipulation — it is accurate commercial intelligence.
closingTechniques.reciprocityClose: Reference all value already provided: free layout plan, showroom visit, sample kit, detailed proposal. This creates psychological obligation without pressure.

discountingRules.neverDiscountFirst: Never reduce price before the full value case is made. Discounting without making the case signals the price was inflated, which destroys trust.
discountingRules.ifDiscountRequired: Trade concessions for commitments: 'If I can get approval for a 5% reduction, can we confirm the order by end of week?'
discountAlternatives: Add value instead of reducing price: include an extra chair, extended warranty registration, complementary furniture disposal
Offer milestone payment structure to reduce cash flow impact
Position finance option to reduce the immediate price objection

legitimate: Lead times: 'Standard lead time is 4–6 weeks. With your move date, we have a 2-week window to confirm before it affects your timeline.'
Installation slots: 'Our Brisbane team is booking 4–6 weeks ahead. I want to hold a slot for you, but I need a confirmed order to do that.'
Price validity: 'This quote is valid for 30 days. Material costs can shift — I can't hold this pricing beyond that.'
urgencyCreation.neverManufacture: Never create artificial urgency. B2B buyers are sophisticated and will detect it. Real urgency is powerful enough.
urgencyCreation.framingRule: Frame urgency around the client's risk ('you may lose your move date slot') not TCD's benefit ('we need the order this week')

internalChampionStrategy.who: Usually the Office Manager, EA, or Facilities Manager — the person coordinating the project day-to-day
internalChampionStrategy.why: They advocate internally, book meetings, and influence the final decision. Their success in getting internal approval = your success.
equip: Proposal summary (1 page) they can forward to CEO/CFO
Comparison summary positioning TCD vs alternatives
ROI framing document (TCO argument for CFO)
internalChampionStrategy.relationship: Check in weekly during the decision period. Be their most helpful external contact. They will feel accountable to the relationship.
